original_question: What is the spectrum of a finite-dimensional random symmetric Bernoulli matrix, meaning a symmetric matrix whose entries are random plus-or-minus one variables subject to the symmetry constraint? In particular, how can one describe the finite-dimensional spectral picture, not just the asymptotic universality behavior known for Wigner ensembles?
target_in_paper: Section 5.3, open problem "Spectrum of a finite-dimensional random symmetric Bernoulli matrix." ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2016/071/sigma16-071.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target: it identifies the ensemble as a symmetric Bernoulli ±1 matrix, keeps the focus on finite-dimensional spectral behavior, and explicitly contrasts this with asymptotic universality for Wigner ensembles, which is exactly how the paper motivates the problem. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2016/071/sigma16-071.pdf))
missing_details: The matrix size should be quantified explicitly: the question is about a fixed but arbitrary finite dimension n, not just an unspecified "finite-dimensional" object.
The ambient setting should be made explicit: a real symmetric n×n matrix B=(b_ij), with b_ij=b_ji.

To be fully stand-alone, the sampling model should be stated explicitly rather than only informally described as "random ±1 subject to symmetry"; at minimum, one should specify that the signs are assigned on and above the diagonal and then reflected by symmetry.
The meaning of "spectrum" should be clarified as the exact fixed-n eigenvalue multiset/spectral law of the ensemble, not the limiting empirical spectral distribution as n→∞.

The paper's key motivation is that, at fixed n, this ensemble has only finitely many eigenvalue configurations; that finite-configuration viewpoint is implicit in your draft and should be stated outright. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2016/071/sigma16-071.pdf))

A faithful reformulation should avoid introducing any normalization such as 1/√n or any asymptotic scaling, since the paper's question is explicitly about the unscaled finite-dimensional picture. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2016/071/sigma16-071.pdf))
refined_question: For each fixed n≥1, let B_n=(b_{ij})_{1≤i,j≤n} be a real symmetric Bernoulli matrix, meaning that b_{ij}=b_{ji} and the entries are random signs ±1 subject to this symmetry constraint. What is the exact finite-n spectral picture of this ensemble—that is, how can one characterize the spectrum (eigenvalue multiset) of a finite-dimensional random symmetric Bernoulli matrix, in a way that captures the genuinely finite-dimensional structure rather than only the asymptotic universality behavior known for Wigner ensembles?
justification: This draft clearly targets §5.3 rather than any theorem- or conjecture-labeled statement elsewhere in the paper. The official formulation in §5.3 asks, almost verbatim, for the spectrum of a finite-dimensional random symmetric Bernoulli matrix, and the surrounding context explains why this is a distinct fixed-size problem: unlike GOE-type ensembles, these matrices have only finitely many eigenvalue configurations at each finite dimension, so general Wigner-universality results address only asymptotics and not the finite-dimensional spectral picture. The rewrite therefore stays narrow, keeps the paper's exact intent, and only adds the minimal stand-alone details the paper leaves implicit: fixed size n, real symmetry, and that the goal is an exact finite-n spectral description. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2016/071/sigma16-071.pdf))
